sam: Heads-up: users hitting "Event loop is closed" at process shutdown when using AsyncClient in uvicorn/gunicorn. Quick repro: create client at module import, serve requests, then worker shutdown.

rita: I've seen that before. Do we spawn background tasks?

sam: Yeah, the client starts a token refresh loop with `asyncio.get_event_loop().create_task(...)` on init and we don't cancel it on aclose(). If aclose() isn't called, shutdown can race and loop is closed.

kevin: Also, our sync Client wrapper calls `asyncio.run()` under the hood which breaks in notebooks (``asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop``). Two related DX bugs: background task lifecycle + sync facade incompatible with nested loops.

sam: Proposed fixes: 1) don't create tasks at import/sync time; create them in async context (`__aenter__`) or only when loop is running. 2) store the Task handle and cancel+await it in `aclose()`; add a finalize warning if not closed. 3) remove internal `asyncio.run()` calls; provide an anyio-backed sync facade and document notebook caveats.

rita: Also add typing for async iterators (`AsyncIterator[Chunk]`) so `async for` autocompletes and tests behave.

kevin: I'll open a draft PR with task cancel + async context manager + tests (pytest-asyncio). tagging infra to run uvicorn shutdown integration in CI.
